source.section: Form 2 PDF p1 lines 1-8 and PDF p2 worksheet lines 1-13; Instructions PDF p12-13 lines 1-8; PDF p17 tax calculation; PDF p18 rate tables; Instructions PDF p13 Line 6, $5,660 subtraction for taxpayers 65 and older; Form 2 PDF p1 line 6; record base.deductions age_65_subtraction; Form 2 PDF p1 lines 3 and 7 ('If zero or less, enter 0'); Instructions PDF p13 Line 7

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = private pension (person 0) 23,000.00 = 23,000.00. Federal taxable income = 23,000.00 - standard deduction 17,750.00 (15,750.00 + 1 x 2,000.00 for 65 or older) = 5,250.00 (federal senior deduction ignored, although Montana's line 2 would take it). Filing status single, no Montana standard deduction or exemptions. Schedule I Part I: line 7 additions 0.00; line 24 subtractions 0.00. Form 2 page 1: line 1 federal AGI 23,000.00; line 2 Form 1040 lines 12e and 13b 17,750.00; line 3 5,250.00; line 4 0.00; line 5 0.00; line 6 age 65 subtraction 1 x 5,660.00 = 5,660.00; line 7 Montana taxable income 5,250.00 + 0.00 - 0.00 - 5,660.00 = -410.00, zero or less, so 0.00. Page 2 worksheet: line 1 taxable income 0.00; no net long-term capital gain, so lines 2-10 are skipped and line 11 is 0.00; line 12 ordinary income tax from the PDF p18 rate table: 4.7% x 0.00 = 0.00; line 13 = 0.00, carried to page 1 line 8. Bracket schedule as numbers (the expected figure): 4.7% x 0.00 = 0.00. Line 9 nonrefundable credits 0.00; line 10 tax after credits 0.00. Household income about 23,000.00 and a person 62 or older: the refundable Elderly Homeowner/Renter Credit (Form 2 line 16) may apply; it is not in the projection and is left out. The subtraction exceeds federal taxable income; line 7 is floored at 0.00.
accepted_approximations: Elderly Homeowner/Renter Credit: refundable, up to 1,150, for age 62 or older with household income under 45,000. Property tax relief outside the record.
